term_glossary.tooltip: Point of interconnection: the utility–facility interface where the specified voltage is measured.
Voltage divided by its nominal reference. A value of 1.00 p.u. is nominal voltage; 0.70 p.u. is 70% of that reference.
Voltage ride-through: the required load behavior during a voltage disturbance, within the specified magnitude and duration limits.
Low-voltage ride-through: performance during voltage sags. Table 1 pairs each sag depth with a minimum duration and permitted power response.
High-voltage ride-through: performance during voltage swells. Table 1 distinguishes the limited constant-power band from the immediate-transfer permission above it.
Post-fault active power recovery: for qualifying low-voltage events, restore 90% of pre-fault computational demand within 2 seconds after voltage returns to 0.90–1.10 p.u.
Power supply unit: equipment that converts incoming electrical power to the supply needed by the IT load. Model, stored-energy and firmware capabilities affect disturbance performance.
Uninterruptible power supply: an energy-storage and power-conversion system used to maintain supply through interruptions. Actual controls and architecture determine its grid-facing response.
Variable-frequency drive: a power-electronic drive that controls a motor’s speed. Cooling-system drives can respond and restart differently from computational loads.
